signals.title: AUD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: AUD/JPY trades at 109.465 amid broad divergence across G10 performance. On the weekly strength scorecard, JPY leads all peers with an average gain of +1.078% across 7 pairs, while AUD anchors the table as the laggard at -0.869% across 4 pairs, creating a critical 1.947% spread. This cross-currency gap expands despite the RBA 4.60% vs BoJ 1.25% policy rate spread offering a nominal 335bp carry advantage to AUD, alongside an overnight AONIA vs TONA carry premium of +337bp. Market focus is overriding this carry differential as BoJ summary of opinions headlines reveal active debate over additional rate hikes to reduce accommodation, clashing with an accommodative JPY real rate of -1.45% vs AUD's +0.60%. Furthermore, AUD/USD trades at 0.6925, sitting beneath its SMA20 at 0.7115, SMA50 at 0.7095, and SMA200 at 0.7031. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/JPY, as cross-asset themes and BoJ normalization momentum overwhelm the nominal carry buffer. Catalyst: Tokyo CPI release at 23:30 UTC. Risk: Sharp risk-on reversal re-engaging carry trades above the 111.00 handle.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew + BoJ Debate
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.178, positioned below its SMA50 at 158.26 and SMA200 at 158.47 while holding above the SMA20 at 156.07. BoJ opinion summaries show policymakers debated raising interest rates further, putting policy normalisation in focus. In options markets, USD/JPY 25-delta risk reversals print at -2.60, marking an extreme put skew that indicates strong demand for downside protection against the dollar. This options positioning stands in contrast to CFTC speculative positioning, where Leveraged Funds hold net long JPY positions of +4,472 contracts at the 98th percentile of their 52-week range (z=+2.66), even after a WoW reduction of 15,597 contracts. Concurrently, 1-month ATM IV sits at 9.2% against an HV30 of 10.0%, generating a negative vol risk premium of -0.8% that highlights structural complacency in realized options pricing. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY, options market positioned for downside retracement against technical resistance. Catalyst: Tokyo CPI release at 23:30 UTC. Risk: A sustained breakout above the 160.00 threshold where BoJ intervention risk previously surfaced.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Yield Divergence + Fiscal Risk
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1235, pinned beneath its SMA20 at 1.1501, SMA50 at 1.1535, and SMA200 at 1.1618. Cross CB differentials structurally anchor the pair, with Fed policy at 4.00% vs ECB at 2.65%, generating a 135bp spread in favor of the dollar, while SOFR at 3.88% vs €STR at 2.44% provides an OIS carry premium of +144bp to USD. Sovereign spreads reflect widening divergence as the DE-US 2Y yield differential sits at -170bp, widening 12bp over 5 sessions and 25bp over 20 sessions in USD's favor. Sell-side research from ING highlights that French budget friction and sovereign bond underperformance leave the euro exposed to further widening pressure. Meanwhile, US 5Y yields stand at 5.06% with the 20-day decomposition (FRED, as of Sep 29) showing a +57bp nominal rise split into real +54bp and breakeven +3bp, indicating real-yield-led dollar support. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, driven by widening rate differentials and sovereign yield drag. Catalyst: Euro Area CPI y/y release at 09:00 UTC. Risk: Core Euro Area inflation printing substantially above the 2.4% forecast.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Extreme Retail Short vs Rate Spread
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4241, maintaining an intact bullish technical posture above its SMA20 at 1.3978, SMA50 at 1.3954, and SMA200 at 1.3848. Retail sentiment from Retail sentiment data displays an extreme imbalance, with 95% of retail accounts holding short positions against only 5% long. This retail bias diverges sharply from institutional futures positioning, where CFTC Leveraged Funds are net short CAD at -49,123 contracts (28.1% long ratio), reflecting net institutional dollar demand. The fundamental backdrop reinforces the institutional stance: Fed at 4.00% vs BoC at 2.25% yields a +175bp nominal carry premium for USD, mirrored by an overnight SOFR vs CORRA carry advantage of +158bp for the dollar. Although WTI crude has advanced 2.92% to $93.1, the large macro policy spread and extreme retail short skew present ongoing short-squeeze risk. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD, supported by central bank carry advantage and retail short exposure. Catalyst: US Nonfarm Payrolls release at 12:30 UTC. Risk: US employment printing significantly below the 52K forecast.
